what: DISPATCHER SELF-HEAL FOR once-UNITS (research-tooling build, for Thursday's plan; NOT built): scripts/research/dispatch_queue.py already has retry guards for a unit with failed history (RETRY_CAP_MARK 'retry cap reached: N landed rows are all non-verdict outcomes (max 2 retries) -- needs a human', UNCHANGED_SINCE_FAILURE_MARK 'deterministic producer_failed, script unchanged'), but they only fire when the unit's last_dispatched_at stamp is absent. While the stamp is present a cadence-once unit reads 'cadence=once and it ran at <ts>' and is never re-evaluated, so a producer_failed-only history strands the unit and the guards never get to decide. MEASURED 2026-11-22 (population: 71 queued cadence-once units whose only result rows are producer_failed, PI-20261122-SME5WDGR-0003): with real stamps all 71 read 'cadence=once and it ran at'; on a temp copy with the stamps cleared the guards would dispatch 46 and refuse 25 (21 at the retry cap, 4 deterministic-unchanged) -- the guards worked, they just never ran. PROPOSED: when a once-unit's landed rows are ALL producer_failed (no measured/verdict row), treat the stamp as not-ran and run the existing guard chain (retry cap, script-unchanged-since-failure, backend/route re-check) to decide re-dispatch vs 'needs a human'; a measured or verdict row keeps the current 'ran' behaviour. Needs: a test with planted failed-only history (re-dispatches when script changed, refuses at cap, refuses when unchanged), byte-identical behaviour for units with any measured row, and a CHECKS-packet line counting failed-only once-units so the pool stays visible. Not a new gate: it only lets the existing guards decide.
